AdapterSettings.description:
The operator's LoRA adapter directory (ADR-0061).

**Empty means off**, deliberately (rule 2): adapters are opt-in, and a default configuration
behaves exactly as it did before adapters existed. The directory holds the served artifacts and
one reviewed ``model.adapter_manifest`` per adapter; FreeWeight reads it and never writes it.

The word "adapter" here is the **LoRA** sense, not the benchmark-harness sense ``[external]``
configures (spec §7.5).

directory.description: Directory holding LoRA artifacts and their reviewed manifests. Empty disables adapters entirely.
directory.title: Directory

AdapterSettings.title: AdapterSettings

AuthSettings.description: Bearer tokens. Empty is the loopback-default, unauthenticated posture (ADR-0014).

tokens.description: Bearer tokens accepted on a non-loopback bind. Secret: never logged, always redacted by config show. Comma-separated in the environment.
tokens.title: Tokens

AuthSettings.title: AuthSettings

BenchmarkSettings.description:
The ``[benchmarks]`` section: limits a machine, not a suite author, decides.

A shipped suite's content is fixed and hashed — that is what makes two runs of it comparable.
What is *not* fixed is how far a sweep can go before the machine running it cannot serve the
context any more, and that is a property of the hardware rather than of the benchmark.

Attributes:
    long_context_max_tokens: The ceiling of ``native.long_context``'s depth sweep. The shipped
        ladder doubles — 2 000, 4 000, 8 000, 16 000, 32 000 — and is truncated to, or extended
        by doubling up to, this value. Raising it on a machine that can serve more turns
        ``effective_context_tokens`` from a floor into a measurement; lowering it on a small
        card keeps the suite runnable instead of failing every rung.

        **It separates results.** The effective ladder is hashed into the suite's
        ``dataset_hashes``, so a 32 000-token sweep and a 128 000-token sweep are two different
        measurements and are never averaged — a sweep that stopped earlier reports a smaller
        effective context for reasons that have nothing to do with the model.
    max_fit_context_tokens: The ceiling of ``native.memory_kv``'s maximum-context-fit ladder,
        ``8 192 … 131 072``, fitted the same way and hashed the same way (ADR-0121 §1). The
        test climbs "until something refuses"; on a provider that spills to host RAM instead
        of refusing, this ceiling is what stops the climb before the machine does.

long_context_max_tokens.description: Ceiling of native.long_context's depth sweep. Hashed into that suite's dataset_hashes, so two ceilings are two measurements.
long_context_max_tokens.title: Long Context Max Tokens

max_fit_context_tokens.description: Ceiling of native.memory_kv's maximum-context-fit ladder (8192 doubling to 131072). Hashed into that suite's dataset_hashes, so two ceilings are two measurements (ADR-0121). Lower it on a provider that spills to host RAM instead of refusing.
max_fit_context_tokens.title: Max Fit Context Tokens

BenchmarkSettings.title: BenchmarkSettings

CalibrationSettings.description:
How judged criteria are calibrated against the author's grades (spec §12).

``n_holdout_target`` is the shrinkage denominator of
[ADR-0032 §2](../../docs/adr/0032-judge-validity-and-user-capability-namespace.md): six
holdout samples at ``kappa_w`` 0.71 yield a validity factor of 0.55, not 0.71. It is
configuration and it is recorded on every calibration report with the policy version, exactly
as ADR-0017's own parameters are.

holdout_fraction.description: Share of graded samples withheld from the jury — the only honest estimate of agreement.
holdout_fraction.title: Holdout Fraction

min_agreement.description: Weighted kappa_w below which a goal emits no evidence at all (ADR-0032 §3).
min_agreement.title: Min Agreement

min_samples.description: Below this many graded samples: CALIBRATION_INSUFFICIENT, not a failed gate.
min_samples.title: Min Samples

partition_seed.description: Seed of the anchor/holdout split, recorded so the split is reproducible.
partition_seed.title: Partition Seed

target_samples.description: How many samples the wizard asks the author to grade.
target_samples.title: Target Samples

CalibrationSettings.title: CalibrationSettings

ConsoleSettings.description:
Where WeightRoomGym is, when one fronts this application (row WM2).

Set, the top bar gains the suite's tab strip: WeightRoomGym itself and the peer applications
through it (``<url>/apps/<name>``), the way the console's own shell links back. Unset — the
default — nothing is rendered, byte for byte as before: an application knows only its own
port, and a strip pointing at loopback addresses another machine cannot reach would be a
strip of dead links.

url.description: WeightRoomGym's base URL (https://<host>:8769); empty renders no application tab strip.
url.title: Url

ConsoleSettings.title: ConsoleSettings

EvidenceSettings.description:
``[evidence]`` — the confidence policy and where the capability weights come from.

Every parameter of ADR-0017's confidence formula, made configuration as that ADR requires, and
recorded on every evidence record beside its ``policy_version`` — so a number computed under one
set of parameters is never silently compared with one computed under another. A customised
parameter produces a *derived* policy version (``1.0+<hash>``), never the shipped one.

``capability_weights_path`` points at a user's own copy of the shipped
``capability_weights.toml`` (benchmark catalog §6). Unset means the shipped file; a custom file
likewise derives its own policy version from its content.

capability_weights_path.description: A custom capability_weights.toml. Unset uses the shipped mapping; a custom file derives its own policy version from its content.
capability_weights_path.title: Capability Weights Path

freshness_floor.description: The lowest the freshness factor can fall. Old evidence degrades rather than vanishes.
freshness_floor.title: Freshness Floor

goal_contribution_weight.description: Weight a goal's composite carries as one source among the shipped ones inside the capability it declares contributes_to (ADR-0032 §1).
goal_contribution_weight.title: Goal Contribution Weight

n_target.description: Sample count at which the sample factor reaches 1.0 (ADR-0017): three samples are worth about 0.32, thirty about 1.0.
n_target.title: N Target

name_only_identity_factor.description: Identity factor for a name-only model identity, whose weights may have changed under the name.
name_only_identity_factor.title: Name Only Identity Factor

performance_drift_factor.description: Environment factor for performance-class evidence after a provider minor change or a driver/CUDA change.
performance_drift_factor.title: Performance Drift Factor

performance_half_life_days.description: Freshness half-life for performance, memory and energy evidence, in days. Speed follows the environment.
performance_half_life_days.title: Performance Half Life Days

quality_drift_factor.description: Environment factor for quality evidence after a provider change with template or sampling implications.
quality_drift_factor.title: Quality Drift Factor

quality_half_life_days.description: Freshness half-life for quality evidence, in days. Quality is stable while the weights are.
quality_half_life_days.title: Quality Half Life Days

stale_below.description: Freshness below which evidence is badged stale and offered a re-run — about one half-life.
stale_below.title: Stale Below

EvidenceSettings.title: EvidenceSettings

ExecutionSettings.description:
Default benchmark execution parameters (spec §12, ``[execution]``).

These are the *application* layer of the second precedence chain spec §12 describes
(application → suite → test → saved settings → run overrides). A run resolves them into its
own ``effective_config`` and freezes that into the run record, so changing a default here
never retroactively changes what an existing run says it did.

The scheduler reads ``warmup_repetitions``, ``measured_repetitions``, ``test_timeout_seconds``,
``run_timeout_seconds``, ``randomize_case_order`` and ``seed``; the idle-detection group and
``cooldown_seconds`` drive the idle-detection outcome of spec §13.

gpu_index.description: The device a run's metrics are attributed to (ADR-0027).
gpu_index.title: Gpu Index

idle_gpu_threshold_percent.description: GPU utilization the machine must be below before measuring; 0 disables the check and records that it was disabled.
idle_gpu_threshold_percent.title: Idle Gpu Threshold Percent

idle_required_samples.description: Consecutive quiet observations required before measuring.
idle_required_samples.title: Idle Required Samples

idle_wait_timeout_seconds.description: How long to wait for the machine to go quiet.
idle_wait_timeout_seconds.title: Idle Wait Timeout Seconds

measured_repetitions.description: How many times each case runs.
measured_repetitions.title: Measured Repetitions

on_idle_timeout.description: What to do when it never does: warn (measure anyway and record measured_while_busy) or refuse.
on_idle_timeout.title: On Idle Timeout

randomize_case_order.description: Shuffle case order within a test.
randomize_case_order.title: Randomize Case Order

seed.description: The seed every randomized decision derives from; recorded on every run.
seed.title: Seed

store_responses.description: Store full response text beside its hash. Off by default (spec §14); goal runs force it on.
store_responses.title: Store Responses

warmup_repetitions.description: Unmeasured generations before the measured ones.
warmup_repetitions.title: Warmup Repetitions

ExecutionSettings.title: ExecutionSettings

ExternalSettings.description:
The ``[external]`` section: where external benchmark environments live (spec §12, ADR-0018).

Every external benchmark gets its own environment under ``root`` — a venv, its datasets and
its recorded install state — entirely separate from FreeWeight's own environment, which never
imports an external benchmark package.

Attributes:
    root: The directory external environments are created under. Unset resolves to
        ``<data>/external``.
    install_timeout_seconds: Wall-clock budget for one environment-creation or
        dataset-download step.
    download_cap_bytes: The most a single dataset download may occupy, enforced while
        streaming — a cap checked after the fact is a cap the disk already paid.

download_cap_bytes.description: Streaming size cap for a single dataset download, in bytes.
download_cap_bytes.title: Download Cap Bytes

install_timeout_seconds.description: Budget for one install or download step, in seconds.
install_timeout_seconds.title: Install Timeout Seconds

root.description: Where external benchmark environments live. Unset resolves to <data>/external.
root.title: Root

ExternalSettings.title: ExternalSettings

GoalSettings.description:
Where user-authored goal packs live, and the bounds on what one may contain (spec §12).

``root`` is deliberately under the *config* directory rather than the data directory: a goal
pack is hand-editable, git-trackable JSON the user owns
([ADR-0031 §6](../../docs/adr/0031-user-defined-goal-benchmarks.md)), not application state.

``max_pack_bytes`` and ``rule_timeout_ms`` are the two bounds spec §14 names on user-authored
content: an import is size-capped before a byte is written, and a criterion's rule runs under
a timeout so a catastrophic pattern fails the criterion rather than the process.

max_pack_bytes.description: Import size cap, enforced before a byte is written.
max_pack_bytes.title: Max Pack Bytes

root.description: Where goal packs live. Unset resolves to <config>/goals.
root.title: Root

rule_timeout_ms.description: Per-criterion, per-sample budget for a rule.
rule_timeout_ms.title: Rule Timeout Ms

GoalSettings.title: GoalSettings

JudgeSettings.description:
The default jury a goal's judged criteria are scored by (spec §12).

Every field here is a *default*; a goal pack's own ``judge`` block overrides it, and the
resolved configuration is a ``goal_hash`` input because a different jury is a different
instrument (ADR-0032 §4).

``allow_remote`` is only half the remote opt-in: ``providers.allow_remote`` is the other half
and both are required (ADR-0031 §4). Neither can be satisfied by accident.

allow_remote.description: Permit a remote juror. Requires providers.allow_remote as well.
allow_remote.title: Allow Remote

blind_candidate_identity.description: Hide the candidate's identity from the jury.
blind_candidate_identity.title: Blind Candidate Identity

jury_size.description: Distinct local models in a jury; 1 disables the jury and says so in the result.
jury_size.title: Jury Size

max_output_tokens.description: Output limit every juror is polled under. Null — the default — lets the provider decide, which is the served context. Set it to make a juror that reasons fail fast instead of spending the whole window; measured too tight at 2048, where a 12B instruct juror lost samples it had been answering (ADR-0141).
max_output_tokens.title: Max Output Tokens

models.description: Juror canonical IDs. Empty selects from the installed models. Comma-separated in the environment.
models.title: Models

randomize_order.description: Randomize the order criteria are presented to a juror in.
randomize_order.title: Randomize Order

refuse_self_judging.description: A juror never judges its own output.
refuse_self_judging.title: Refuse Self Judging

repetitions.description: How many times each juror grades each criterion.
repetitions.title: Repetitions

temperature.description: Sampling temperature every juror is polled at.
temperature.title: Temperature

JudgeSettings.title: JudgeSettings

format.description: text, json, or auto (text on a TTY, json otherwise).
format.title: Format

include_content.description: Log full prompts and responses. Off by default: only hashes and lengths are logged (observability standards §3.2).
include_content.title: Include Content

ProviderSettings.description:
The default model provider FreeWeight talks to.

One provider, not a registry. FreeWeight measures one machine's models one run at a time: it
has no candidate pool and no scoring, so it has nothing to disambiguate between registrations
and no use for LoadCoach's `[providers.<name>]` table
(ADR-0077). That divergence is deliberate; a
second provider here would be its own phase with its own evidence.

Three keys serve ``kind = "llamacpp"`` and nothing else, because Ollama needs none of them:
llama.cpp is a server FreeWeight launches and supervises over a directory of GGUF weights
(ADR-0062), where Ollama is a
daemon that already knows where its models are.

base_url.description: The provider's API endpoint. Ignored by kind='llamacpp'.
base_url.title: Base Url

kind.description: Which provider serves the models: ollama, llamacpp, or fake for tests.
kind.title: Kind

memory_high_bytes.description: The throttle point below memory_max_bytes (MemoryHigh). Requires memory_max_bytes and must be below it.
memory_high_bytes.title: Memory High Bytes

memory_max_bytes.description: Host-memory cap for every llama-server this application launches (ADR-0119): the launch runs in a systemd-run user scope with MemoryMax at this value and swap denied, so a server that does not fit is killed rather than swapping the host. llamacpp only; unset launches uncapped.
memory_max_bytes.title: Memory Max Bytes

model_directory.description: Directory of GGUF weights kind='llamacpp' serves. Required for that kind; there is no default worth guessing, because a wrong directory is a server serving weights nobody asked for.
model_directory.title: Model Directory

server_path.description: The llama-server executable, resolved on PATH unless absolute.
server_path.title: Server Path

state_dir.description: Where the llama.cpp supervisor keeps its pid files and digest cache. Empty means <data_dir>/llamacpp.
state_dir.title: State Dir

ProviderSettings.title: ProviderSettings

ProvidersSettings.description: Cross-provider policy, distinct from the single default provider's own settings.

allow_remote.description: Permit a remote provider at all. One half of the remote-judging opt-in; judge.allow_remote is the other (ADR-0031 §4).
allow_remote.title: Allow Remote

ProvidersSettings.title: ProvidersSettings

RuntimeSettings.description:
``[runtime]`` — how a model is loaded and served, as opposed to how a run is executed.

ADR-0023's runtime profile, made settable. It is a **separate section from ``[execution]``**
because the two are separate axes and are separated everywhere else: an execution parameter
(repetitions, seed, cooldown) is how a measurement is taken, while a runtime setting is what is
being measured *under*. They hash into the fingerprint through different fields —
``execution.effective_parameters`` and ``runtime_profile_hash`` — and ADR-0017 makes a differing
runtime profile a **hard separation**, not a discount: evidence measured at one context does not
describe another.

Every field defaults to ``None``, which is the legal profile meaning "provider defaults"
(ADR-0023 §1). There is no "no profile" state; ``RuntimeProfile()`` has a stable hash and is
stored like any other.

**Only settings the configured provider can actually honour appear in a profile.** Flash
attention and KV-cache precision are launch-time settings ``llama-server`` honours per model;
Ollama reads them once, daemon-wide (``OLLAMA_FLASH_ATTENTION``, ``OLLAMA_KV_CACHE_TYPE``),
so under ``provider.kind = "ollama"`` either key is **refused by name** rather than recorded
as a promise the run cannot keep — the dishonesty ADR-0007 rule 2 forbids of a capability
flag, applied to a profile (ADR-0120).

Attributes:
    context_size: The context to serve, in tokens — Ollama's ``num_ctx``. Unset means the
        provider decides, and the run records its served context as ``assumed`` rather than
        ``configured``. **Setting it is what makes a context comparison possible**: two runs of
        one model at two contexts are two subjects, and without this they are indistinguishable.
    flash_attention: Whether the server is launched with flash attention. llama.cpp only.
    kv_cache_precision: The KV cache's precision — ``f16``, ``q8_0`` or ``q4_0``. llama.cpp
        only. A quantized cache **requires** ``flash_attention = true``: llama.cpp cannot
        quantize the V cache without it and silently keeps f16 otherwise, which would record a
        precision that was never served. A different precision is a different
        ``runtime_profile_hash`` and therefore a different measurement subject (ADR-0017).
    fit_to_device: Whether ``llama-server`` may adjust unset launch arguments to fit device
        memory (its ``--fit on`` default). ``False`` — FreeWeight's default — launches with
        ``--fit off``: a profile that does not fit fails at launch and is recorded as that
        failure, rather than spilling layers to host RAM under a profile hash that says
        nothing about the spill (ADR-0121). Travels as ``provider_options["--fit"]`` and is
        hashed like every other launch fact. Ignored under any other provider kind.
    gpu_layers: Layers to offload to the GPU. Unset lets the provider fit it.
    threads: CPU threads for the parts that stay on the host.
    batch_size: Prompt-evaluation batch size.
    keep_alive: How long the provider should hold the model resident after a call, in its own
        duration syntax. A benchmark that reloads between every test measures loading.

context_size.description: Context window to serve, in tokens (Ollama's num_ctx). Unset lets the provider decide and records the served context as assumed. A different value is a different measurement subject (ADR-0023).
context_size.title: Context Size

fit_to_device.description: Let llama-server shrink unset launch arguments to fit device memory (--fit on). False launches with --fit off: no fit is a launch failure, never a host-RAM spill (ADR-0121). llamacpp only.
fit_to_device.title: Fit To Device

flash_attention.description: Launch the server with flash attention. Honoured by provider.kind='llamacpp' only; refused by name under 'ollama', whose setting is daemon-wide (ADR-0120).
flash_attention.title: Flash Attention

gpu_layers.description: Layers offloaded to the GPU. Unset lets the provider fit them.
gpu_layers.title: Gpu Layers

keep_alive.description: How long the provider holds the model resident after a call, in the provider's own duration syntax.
keep_alive.title: Keep Alive

kv_cache_precision.description: KV-cache precision: f16, q8_0 or q4_0. llamacpp only; q8_0 and q4_0 require flash_attention = true. A different precision is a different measurement subject.
kv_cache_precision.title: Kv Cache Precision

threads.description: CPU threads for the parts that stay on the host.
threads.title: Threads

RuntimeSettings.title: RuntimeSettings

SandboxSettings.description:
The ``[sandbox]`` section: how model-generated code is contained (spec §12, ADR-0018).

The tiers are container → bwrap → **refuse**, and there is no host tier and no flag to create
one. ``tier`` can only hold the selection *at or below* what the machine offers: naming a tier
that is unavailable is a refusal at run time, never a silent fall-through to a weaker one —
a user who wrote ``container`` asked for a container's guarantees, and handing them bwrap's
instead would be a security decision made on their behalf.

Attributes:
    tier: ``auto`` (highest available), ``container``, ``bwrap``, or ``none``. ``none``
        disables code execution entirely: every benchmark that needs a sandbox is skipped
        with ``sandbox_unavailable``.
    cpu_limit: CPU cores the sandboxed process may use (container ``--cpus`` /
        bwrap-tier rlimit).
    memory_limit_mb: Address-space cap for sandboxed execution.
    timeout_seconds: Wall-clock budget per sandboxed invocation; the process is killed when
        it is exceeded.

cpu_limit.description: CPU cores a sandboxed process may use.
cpu_limit.title: Cpu Limit

memory_limit_mb.description: Memory cap for sandboxed execution, in MiB.
memory_limit_mb.title: Memory Limit Mb

tier.description: Sandbox tier for code-execution benchmarks: auto = highest available; container and bwrap select exactly that tier or refuse; none refuses all code execution.
tier.title: Tier

timeout_seconds.description: Wall-clock budget per sandboxed invocation, in seconds.
timeout_seconds.title: Timeout Seconds

SandboxSettings.title: SandboxSettings

allow_lan_exposure.description: Acknowledges a deliberate bind to every interface (0.0.0.0). Without it such a bind refuses to start.
allow_lan_exposure.title: Allow Lan Exposure

allowed_hosts.description: Host header values accepted on a non-loopback bind, against DNS rebinding. Comma-separated in the environment.
allowed_hosts.title: Allowed Hosts

host.description: Interface to bind. Loopback by default; anything else requires allowed_hosts and auth.tokens (ADR-0026).
host.title: Host

port.description: TCP port for the web UI and the API.
port.title: Port

StorageSettings.description:
Database and artifact locations.

``config show``/``config init`` present the full picture of what a fresh install would use,
per Configuration Standards §5.

artifact_dir.description: Where run artifacts (raw responses, generated code, exports) are written. Unset resolves under the XDG data directory.
artifact_dir.title: Artifact Dir

auto_migrate.description: Migrate on startup. Unset means true on SQLite and false on PostgreSQL, where a failed migration cannot be rolled back automatically (database standards §5.1).
auto_migrate.title: Auto Migrate

backup_retention.description: Automatic pre-migration backups kept before the oldest is rotated away.
backup_retention.title: Backup Retention

database_url.description: SQLAlchemy URL. Unset resolves to a SQLite file under the XDG data directory; PostgreSQL is the other supported dialect (ADR-0006).
database_url.title: Database Url

statement_timeout_ms.description: PostgreSQL statement (and lock) timeout. Unset leaves the server default; SQLite uses its own busy timeout, which the engine always sets.
statement_timeout_ms.title: Statement Timeout Ms

StorageSettings.title: StorageSettings

TelemetrySettings.description: Sampling behaviour for the (Phase 4) telemetry bar and (Phase 6) run recording.

calibrate_overhead.description: Measure what sampling itself costs before a run, and record it on the run.
calibrate_overhead.title: Calibrate Overhead

interval_ms.description: How often the sampler reads the host and the GPUs. Recorded on every run as a measurement condition.
interval_ms.title: Interval Ms

persist_during_runs.description: Store the telemetry series beside a run so its charts survive a restart.
persist_during_runs.title: Persist During Runs

TelemetrySettings.title: TelemetrySettings

json_schema.description:
The complete, validated FreeWeight configuration.

Constructed only by :func:`load_settings`, which resolves the precedence chain first — never
call ``Settings(**raw_dict)`` directly on unmerged input, or the file/env/CLI layering in
Configuration Standards §1 is bypassed.
json_schema.title: Settings

runtime_changeable.description: How often the machine telemetry sampler reads the host and the GPUs. Lower is more detail and more overhead; the overhead is measured and recorded on every run.
Store the telemetry series alongside a run, so its charts survive a restart.
Measure what sampling itself costs before a run, and record it on the run. Turning this off does not make sampling free; it makes its cost unrecorded.
Unmeasured generations before the measured ones, to reach a warm state.
How many times each case runs. More repetitions, tighter dispersion.
Idle gap between tests, so one test's heat is not the next test's result.
Shuffle case order within a test, so position cannot become a result.
The seed every randomized decision derives from. Recorded in every run.
Utilization the GPU must be below before a run is measured. 0 disables the check and records that it was disabled.
What to do when the GPU never goes idle: warn and measure anyway, recording measured_while_busy, or refuse to measure at all.
How many automatic backups to keep before rotating the oldest away.
Log verbosity for the running server.
